name: Vaping duty-stamp activation and traceability software
demand: The compliance trigger is real: from 1 January 2027 only digital stamps may be affixed, and by 1 April 2027 products outside duty suspension must carry a stamp (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-vaping-duty-stamps-work). HMRC estimated 200 manufacturers and up to 750 importers and warehousekeepers, while warning the taxpayer population is uncertain; it expected the duty’s administrative impact to be negligible, though it expects the combined duty and stamp scheme to have a significant effect (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/introduction-of-vaping-products-duty-from-1-october-2026/introduction-of-vaping-products-duty-from-1-october-2026). Google Play showed 10+ installs for each Cartor app when checked on 23 October 2026; this is an Android store floor, not a count of businesses or paid users (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=uk.co.vdscartor.sdas; https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=uk.co.vdscartor.lote). Search volume, actual approved-business counts, willingness to pay, and software adoption are unverified.
prices: VapeTax’s homepage advertises £149/£500/£999 monthly plans, or annual equivalents of £119.20/£400/£799.20 monthly, plus a £98 camera and £19,788 stamp machine; these are listed prices, not evidence of paid sales (https://vapetax.co.uk/). Its terms, last updated 3 July 2026, instead list Free/£249 Business/£1,499 Enterprise, so its published pricing is inconsistent (https://vapetax.co.uk/terms). Cartor’s two official apps are listed as free; Cartor’s portal/API pricing is unverified (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/uk-vds-sdas/id6805026080; https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/uk-vds-logistic-traceability/id6806295010).

revenue_proof.claim: No verified customer payment or SaaS revenue for VapeTax or a proposed entrant found in the reviewed material; the terms describe advance billing through Stripe, which does not prove a transaction occurred.

Adjacent public-spend signal, not entrant revenue: an HMRC contract notice published 10 February 2026 estimates £32 million excluding VAT for the stamp-scheme concession over five years plus an optional year, and says about one-third relates to non-profitable delivery costs. This is an estimate for the appointed scheme, not realized software receipts.

copy_speed: The official competitor has already shipped the core workflows: Apple lists Cartor SDAS version 1.0 on 17 September 2026 and version 1.0.1 on 8 October; the app declares and activates stamps (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/uk-vds-sdas/id6805026080). Cartor’s LOTE app records and tracks movements; Google Play lists its initial version and a 7 September 2026 update (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=uk.co.vdscartor.lote). VapeTax is another direct competitor publicly evidenced by terms dated 3 July 2026; its company Qode Ltd was incorporated on 3 June 2026, but VapeTax’s exact launch date is unverified (https://vapetax.co.uk/terms; https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/17259547). No other third-party launches since April 2026 were verified.
platform_risk: Very high for the proposed activation-and-traceability core. Cartor/SICPA already supplies SDAS activation and LOTE traceability apps, and Cartor says operators must use its software or API for relevant movement records (https://cartor.com/vaping-duty-stamp-programme/; https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/uk-vds-sdas/id6805026080; https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/uk-vds-logistic-traceability/id6806295010). The LOTE API key is supplied by SICPA, and its published specification says its material may not be used to develop or market a product or service without SICPA’s express written permission (https://cartor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/UK-LOTE-API-Technical-Specifications-v1.7-EN.pdf). SICPA’s July FAQ says master-data maintenance has no API and is handled through its portal; some setup is manual (https://cartor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CO00045.pdf). Get written commercial-use and integration permission before building against these materials.
defensible_asset: Weak at launch: HMRC’s required product fields and duty rules are public, and the scheme API uses documented EPCIS events (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-vaping-duty-stamps-work; https://cartor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/UK-LOTE-API-Technical-Specifications-v1.7-EN.pdf). Customer-approved ERP integrations, exception handling, and validated product mappings could become useful assets, but are unproven and dependent on SICPA access. VapeTax’s terms say customers own their records and can export backups, limiting any assumed data lock-in (https://vapetax.co.uk/terms).
build_effort: A basic adapter, event queue with retries, product/SKU ledger, and reconciliation/export layer is a plausible technical scope because LOTE exposes an event API and asynchronous processing (https://cartor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/UK-LOTE-API-Technical-Specifications-v1.7-EN.pdf). A reliable commercial estimate is unverified until SICPA grants written permission, sandbox credentials are obtained, and the integration is exercised; production use also entails auditability and handling rejected or anomalous events (https://cartor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CO00045.pdf; https://cartor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/UK-LOTE-API-Technical-Specifications-v1.7-EN.pdf).
channel: Use inbound search content and free product/SKU preflight tools, plus opt-in webinars or referrals from ERP, excise-accounting, and logistics partners; Cartor publishes guidance and integration materials that can inform useful educational content (https://cartor.com/vaping-duty-stamp-programme/). For a first validation, contact only verified incorporated businesses at generic corporate addresses, identify the sender, and provide an opt-out; ICO guidance says PECR consent rules for unsolicited email do not apply to corporate subscribers, while sole traders and some partnerships are individual subscribers requiring consent or a valid soft opt-in (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/).
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; the business is a proposal, and no operating record demonstrates Ricardo can keep it within 5 hours per week.
desk_test: One-day, no-code go/no-go: map Cartor’s existing activation and movement workflows from its public guides, mock one missing ERP-to-LOTE reconciliation screen, and send a conditional paid-pilot offer to verified incorporated manufacturers/importers using only generic corporate addresses. Ask SICPA/Cartor for written commercial integration permission at the same time. Treat a buyer commitment and written permission as required evidence before building; give each email sender identification and an opt-out, and exclude sole traders and individual contacts (https://cartor.com/vaping-duty-stamp-programme/; https://cartor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/UK-LOTE-API-Technical-Specifications-v1.7-EN.pdf; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/).
red_flags: The cheap kill-check missed a major platform/IP blocker: the official supplier already performs activation and movement tracking, and SICPA’s API specification expressly restricts commercial development based on its material without written permission (https://cartor.com/vaping-duty-stamp-programme/; https://cartor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/UK-LOTE-API-Technical-Specifications-v1.7-EN.pdf). The addressable regulated population is limited and uncertain; HMRC described duty administration impact as negligible (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/introduction-of-vaping-products-duty-from-1-october-2026/introduction-of-vaping-products-duty-from-1-october-2026). A direct competitor advertises the same broad category of records and production workflow, but actual sales remain unverified (https://vapetax.co.uk/; https://vapetax.co.uk/terms). No 50% automation or <=5-hour weekly workload has been demonstrated; both remain unverified.
